items.informal_name: Square root function on real numbers
items.informal_description: For any real number $ x $, the function returns the principal (non-negative) square root of $ \max(x, 0) $, ensuring the result is a non-negative real number by first mapping $ x $ to the non-negative reals and then applying the square root.

items.informal_name: Square root of a real number
items.informal_description: The function that maps a non-negative real number $ x $ to its principal square root $ \sqrt{x} $.

items.informal_name: NormNum Extension for Real Square Roots
items.informal_description: An instance of the NormNumExt structure that extends the norm_num tactic to evaluate real square roots, enabling normalization of numeric expressions involving square roots of real numbers during automated proof construction.
For any real number $x$, the square root of $x^2$ is equal to $\max(x, 0)$.

items.informal_name: Derivative of Square Root Function at Non-Zero Points
items.informal_description: The square root function $ f(x) = \sqrt{\max(x, 0)} $ has derivative $ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} $ at every real number $ x \neq 0 $. This derivative is defined for all real numbers except zero, where the function's behavior changes from constant zero (for $ x < 0 $) to increasing (for $ x > 0 $).

items.type:

items.informal_description: For an element $ a $ in a non-unital $^*$-ring $ A $ equipped with a non-unital continuous functional calculus structure over $ \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} $, this function computes the square root of $ a $ by applying the continuous functional calculus map $ \text{cfc}_\mathbb{R} $ to the non-negative real square root function $ \sqrt{\cdot} $. Specifically, it returns $ \text{cfc}_\mathbb{R}(\sqrt{\cdot})(a) $, which corresponds to the square root of $ a $ in the context of the functional calculus framework.
